name: Pastel Red
lede: Pastel Red is a soft, chalky red, a red lightened and made a little powdery.

sections.title: Fondant pink
sections.body:
The name is descriptive: a red in the pastel manner [3]. Paterson's dictionary uses the same words for another name, calling fondant pink a pastel red [1]. That shows how dictionaries describe a pale or soft red by comparison rather than by pigment [1].

No book we hold gives Pastel Red a history of its own [3]. Colors it sits near include [[coral]] and [[indian-red]] [3].

The swatch on this page is #DB5856, the screen value we hold for it, which is an approximation and not a measured pigment [3]. Like any pale color it sits between its hue and [[white]], and because the name is a description and not a tradition, other lists may place it a little differently [3].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: Pastel Red appears in 46 of the 23,781 paintings in our archive, about 0.19 percent, as photographed [2]. It peaks in the 1900s, found in 6 of the 1,674 paintings from that century, about 1.7 times the museums' baseline rate [2].
